text:
evan: New user report: our web-starter crashes during onboarding after the recent exports map cleanup. They hit ERR_REQUIRE_ESM on Node and Vite errors in dev.

ev an: Repro (from user): git clone examples/web-starter && cd examples/web-starter && npm ci && npm run dev -> vite aborts.

maya: Can you paste the error?

ev an: Vite error: Failed to resolve import "@redwood/inference-sdk/client" from /src/main.ts: package.json subpath './client' is not defined. Also user tried node dist/server.js and saw TypeError [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: Must use import to load ES Module: /workspace/node_modules/@redwood/inference-sdk/dist/client.mjs

nik: Oof. What does the SDK package.json exports look like now?

ev an: Published snippet user provided: 
```json
{"name":"@redwood/inference-sdk","version":"1.8.0","main":"dist/client.cjs.js","exports":{"./client":"dist/client.cjs.js"},"files":["dist"]}
```

maya: That explains it. We removed the conditional mapping and shipped only the CJS path under the subpath, but earlier publishes had an mjs import path. Consumers and bundlers are now in a split state. Some bundlers follow the exports map strictly and can't see the top-level module field. Others will try import semantics and get the mjs file elsewhere -> ERR_REQUIRE_ESM.

nik: Also likely a TS/IDE resolution mismatch: users see auto-imports point to '@redwood/inference-sdk/client' while types are not present under that subpath so tsc/tsserver substitutes another path -> runtime surprises.

ev an: User's package.json in example used "@redwood/inference-sdk/client" as a subpath import. They expected both require+import to work.

maya: Quick patch: add conditional exports for the subpath and include the types path. Example: 
```json
"exports": {
  "./client": {
    "import": "./dist/client.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/client.cjs.js",
    "types": "./dist/client.d.ts"
  }
}
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```
This covers Node import, CommonJS require, and TS resolution.

nik: Also note pnpm workspace local links can mask this problem during internal dev because the workspace package may use a sibling build that still had both files. We need an examples smoke test that installs the package the way consumers do (npm pack / from-registry) not workspace:link.

evan: Agreed. Can we add a CI matrix that does: npm pack -> install into example, then run: node -e "require('@redwood/inference-sdk/client')", node --input-type=module -e "import('@redwood/inference-sdk/client')", vite dev build, and tsc --noEmit?

maya: Yes. Also add a lightweight esbuild bundle check because many users use esbuild-based bundlers in deploy pipelines.

nik: For edge runtimes (Vercel/Cloudflare), they prefer ESM; if we ship only CJS at a subpath, deploys will fail. Add a blurb to onboarding docs: "When publishing, ensure subpath exports include both import and require targets; prefer explicit .mjs/.cjs extensions to avoid flipping top-level \"type\" unexpectedly."

arya: Small gotcha: some TS versions (older) require types to be exposed in the exports map for subpath imports to resolve in editors. We should add the types field inside the subpath export to avoid weird editor auto-imports.

build-bot: CI: examples/pack-install -> exports-compat-check failed on step 2 (node import check).

evan: I'll open a patch to restore conditional exports + types and add the CI matrix. I will also add a short troubleshooting note in examples/README showing both usage patterns: `const client = require('@redwood/inference-sdk/client')` and `import client from '@redwood/inference-sdk/client'` and a quick npm pack smoke test for maintainers.

maya: When you open the PR include a short migration note in CHANGELOG and mention the pnpm workspace masking risk. Also add a GH action that runs the pack-install matrix on publish PRs.

evan: On it. Tagging @nik for review.

nik: thanks. One follow-up: can we create a pre-publish lint that validates every exported subpath has both import and require keys (or at least warns)? That would have caught this.

maya: Good idea. We can implement as an npm script + node script that runs in CI pre-publish. Add to the backlog if PR scope gets big.

evan: PR incoming (draft). Will include tests and docs.
